public_rationale: Marcus forecast that a whole generation of children would soon be educated by plausible but wrong AI videos. Reporting from February 2026, summarising a New York Times review, says YouTube recommends nonsensical AI videos labelled as educational to toddlers and preschoolers. That fits his worry. But no representative data shows that such videos have become a generation-wide source of learning. The claim also has no deadline. It stays open.
limitations: The scope words ('whole generation', 'educated by') are hard to measure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Soon, a whole generation of children will be educated by AI-generated fake videos that look plausible to naive viewers but are factually incorrect.

statement.excerpt: We are about to have a whole generation of children educated by fake videos that are completely plausible to naive audiences yet biologically (or physically or culturally, etc) incorrect.
statement.document_title: Absolutely amazing ant video augurs intellectual mayhem

from_speaker: biologically (or physically or culturally, etc) incorrect
our_interpretation: Read plainly: soon, AI-made fake videos with factual errors would become a large, generation-wide source of learning for children.
'About to' gives no fixed deadline. A few reports of children being shown such videos would not by themselves show that a whole generation is being educated by them.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence, such as surveys or large studies, that AI-generated videos with factual errors have become a major way children in general learn.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence after a reasonable period showing that such videos remain a minor part of what children watch to learn.

evidence.excerpt: The review found that YouTube often promotes strange, nonsensical videos from channels that purport to teach toddlers and preschoolers the alphabet and animals.
evidence.explanation: Shows that 'educational' AI videos with false content are being recommended to young children. It does not show how many children learn from them, so it cannot settle a 'whole generation' claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative surveys or platform data on the share of children's educational viewing that is AI-generated and factually wrong.
